title: Working at Redwood — Onboarding, Careers, Benefits & Internal Tools (2026 Update)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose

This update consolidates core People Ops guidance for working at Redwood: culture and expectations, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, the hiring and onboarding workflow, and a practical quick-start for the internal tools new hires use every day. It's intended as a single reference for new employees, managers, and hiring partners.

1) Culture & expectations

Overview:
- Mission-aligned work: prioritize product stability, predictable inference economics, and developer ergonomics.
- Core behaviors: ownership, iteration, clarity in communication, and empathy for customers and colleagues.
- Work model: hybrid by default (up to two remote days per week). Team-level policies may vary and are recorded in team handbooks.

Day-to-day expectations:
- Ship small, testable increments and document design decisions in Confluence.
- Use feature flags and rollout plans for user-facing changes.
- Instrument services: add metrics, alerts, and dashboards for any production change.
- Be proactive about career development: discuss goals during quarterly check-ins.

2) Roles & career ladders (summary)

Role families covered here: Engineering (Backend, Serving Runtime, Infra, SRE, DevEx), Product, Research & Applied ML, DevRel, Customer Success, Sales/Go-to-Market, People Ops, Finance, Legal, Security.

Common levels (engineer-focused):
- IC1 / New Grad: focused on learning, delivers scoped tasks with mentorship.
- IC2 / Software Engineer: independently delivers medium-scope features; owns testing and documentation.
- IC3 / Senior Engineer: drives design, mentors others, and improves team reliability.
- IC4 / Staff Engineer: leads cross-team projects, defines architecture, influences roadmaps.
- IC5+ / Principal/Distinguished: shapes company-level technical strategy.

Promotion principles (applies to all functions):
- Evidence-based: promotions require a promotion packet with concrete examples of impact.
- Readiness: consistent ownership, influence beyond immediate scope, and demonstrated mentorship.
- Timing: no fixed clock; typical range 12-24 months depending on impact.
- Process: manager prepares packet, collates peer feedback, and submits to the Calibration Committee.

Manager tips:
- Keep a running examples doc for direct reports with impact and complexity notes.
- Run quarterly career conversations and set measurable goals.
- Use the Promotion Packet template in the PeopleOps Portal.

3) Benefits & perks (high-level summary)

Redwood provides a competitive, regionally-adjusted benefits package. Contact People Ops for country-specific plans and enrollment windows.

Core offerings (US & EMEA highlights):
- Medical, dental, vision plans with employer contributions.
- Retirement: 401(k) with employer match (US); local equivalents in EMEA.
- Parental leave: up to 18 weeks for primary caregivers, 8 weeks for secondary caregivers (paid).
- Paid time off: baseline 20 days PTO + 10 company holidays; wellness days.
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual stipend per employee.
- Home office stipend and equipment reimbursement.
- Equity: RSU grants at hire with periodic refreshes for high performers.
- Mental health support through EAP and wellness subsidies.

Enrollment & support:
- New hires receive enrollment instructions on Day 1 via the PeopleOps Portal.
- For questions: hr@redwood.ai.

4) Hiring process (concise guide for hiring managers)

High-level process:
1. Requisition & approval: create role in Greenhouse with a clear scorecard.
2. Sourcing & shortlist: recruiting partners with hiring manager to present candidates.
3. Intro screen: 30-40 minute call to assess fundamentals and alignment.
4. Technical/role screen: small take-home or live exercise (<=3 hours).
5. Interview loop: 3-5 interviews using structured rubrics.
6. Offer: recruiter prepares offer within compensation bands; Finance reviews for approval.
7. Background checks & preboarding.

Interview best practices:
- Use the scorecard and structured questions.
- Ensure interviewers submit feedback within 48 hours.
- Assemble diverse panels where possible.

5) Onboarding & first 90 days

Pre-boarding (after offer acceptance):
- Welcome kit and Day 1 agenda sent by Recruiting.
- Manager completes New Hire Setup form (PeopleOps Portal) including access, equipment, and buddy assignment.

Day 1 essentials:
- Accounts: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, GitHub, Jira, PeopleOps Portal.
- Device shipped & home-office stipend instructions.
- Mandatory compliance trainings scheduled.
- First-week goals and 30/60/90 plan shared.

Suggested 30/60/90 milestones:
- 30 days: complete trainings, meet core collaborators, fix or document a small issue.
- 60 days: own a small feature or reliable operational task; run a team demo.
- 90 days: deliver measurable impact and present learnings + next goals.

Manager checklist (first 2 weeks):
- Schedule weekly 1:1s and set expectations.
- Assign mentor/buddy and schedule knowledge transfer sessions.
- Provide a clear first project with acceptance criteria.

6) Internal tools quick guide

Tools you will use and where to start:
- Slack: primary communication. Join #onboarding and your team channels.
- Confluence: documentation, ADRs, and templates (PRD, ADR, Postmortem).
- GitHub: code, branch protection, CODEOWNERS; onboarding repo available on first day.
- Jira: issue tracking and team backlogs; use component tags.
- PeopleOps Portal: HR self-service (benefits, time off, promotion templates).
- Okta & MFA: identity provider; enable MFA on Day 1.
- Redwood Console (internal): monitoring, deployments, and feature flags (role-based access).
- Ramp/Expense: corporate card and expense submission.
- IT Self-Service: device requests, VPN, and special software access.

Quick-start checklist for new hires:
1. Complete Okta registration and enable MFA.
2. Join #onboarding and relevant team Slack channels.
3. Confirm GitHub access and fork the onboarding repo.
4. Verify access to the PeopleOps Portal and complete benefits enrollment.

7) Manager playbook snippets

Hiring & scaling advice:
- Define the team mission and 90-day outcomes before creating the req.
- Use scorecards to keep hiring decisions level-appropriate.
- Plan overlap time for early hires and ensure documentation is available.
- Assume 6-8 weeks for ramp to full productivity on complex infra work.
